I'm also realizing both GCC's gnu++20 default and nvcc's fmad=true both contract multiply-adds into FMA with -march=native, so matching that behavior on the GPU side could actually let me get bit-exact results between CPU and GPU.\n\nSince exact bit-matching isn't guaranteed anyway, I'll lean toward a warp-per-row CSR-vector kernel for better scalability, accepting that reordered reduction introduces tiny floating-point differences that tolerance-based validation should absorb.\n\nI should keep the CPU reference computation and the sequential matrix initialization (with its rand() seed) untouched as the golden oracle, since only the timed benchmark kernel needs to be the CUDA-parallelized piece.\n\nFor timing, I'll mirror the original's structure: transfer data to device, time the kernel loop with proper synchronization, and copy the result back once at the end rather than per-iteration, keeping the same millisecond output format so results stay comparable.\n\nI'm also weighing whether to add a warm-up kernel launch before timing starts, since GPU context initialization overhead could otherwise skew the first measurement significantly.\n\nFor the kernel itself, I'm going with a CSR-vector approach using a warp per row, which suits the moderate nonzero density well, using read-only cache loads and a block size of 256 threads.\n\nI'm using uint32_t as the index type throughout, and also considering edge cases like zero items from an empty matrix or extreme sparsity, and whether zero-byte cudaMalloc behaves safely.\n\nKernel launches with a grid size of zero would error with an invalid configuration, so I need to guard against numRows==0 by skipping GPU launches entirely while still letting the host-side path run harmlessly with empty vectors and zero-byte memcpys.\n\nI should add a CUDA_CHECK macro for error handling and figure out the CMake setup — enabling the CUDA language and setting architectures. Since the vector is only 8KB, I don't need constant memory or textures — relying on __ldg for read-only caching should be sufficient.\n\nFor the GPU side, I'll keep spmvCpu as the reference and add spmvKernel plus a spmvGpu host wrapper, looping launches rather than bothering with CUDA graphs since that would be overkill for just a few iterations.  // 8 warps per block\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Macro: CUDA_CHECK\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Abort with a diagnostic message if a CUDA runtime call fails\n// ****************************************************************************\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                        \\\n    do {                                                                        \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call); i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i] = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initRandomMatrix\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Assigns random positions to a given number of elements in a square\n//   matrix. The function encodes these positions in compressed sparse\n//   row (CSR) format.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   cols:          array for column indexes of elements (size should be = n)\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   n:             number of nonzero elements\n//   dim:           number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid initRandomMatrix(index_t* cols, index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t n, const index_t dim) {\n    index_t nnzAssigned = 0;\n\n    // Figure out the probability that a nonzero should be assigned\n    double prob = static_cast<double>(n) / (static_cast<double>(dim) * static_cast<double>(dim));\n\n    // Seed random number generator\n    srand(8675309);\n\n    // Randomly decide whether entry i,j gets a value, but ensure n values are assigned\n    bool fillRemaining = false;\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        rowDelimiters[i] = nnzAssigned;\n        for (index_t j = 0; j < dim; ++j) {\n            index_t numEntriesLeft = (dim * dim) - ((i * dim) + j);\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\n                fillRemaining = true;\n            }\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                cols[nnzAssigned] = j;\n                nnzAssigned++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    // Convention: put the number of non-zeroes at the end of the row delimiters array\n    rowDelimiters[dim] = n;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvCpu\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Computes sparse matrix-vector multiplication using CSR format on the host.\n//   Serves as the independent reference for validation.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val: array holding the non-zero values for the matrix\n//   cols: array of column indices for each element\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   vec: dense vector of size dim to be used for multiplication\n//   dim: number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//   out: output - result from the spmv calculation\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\n             const double* vec, const index_t dim, double* out) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Kernel: spmvCsrVectorKernel\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Computes sparse matrix-vector multiplication using CSR format on the GPU.\n//   One warp is assigned to each row: the 32 lanes stride over the row's\n//   nonzeros (coalesced loads of val/cols), then the partial sums are reduced\n//   with warp shuffles and lane 0 writes the row result.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val, cols, rowDelimiters, vec, dim, out: as in spmvCpu (device pointers)\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void spmvCsrVectorKernel(const double* __restrict__ val,\n                                    const index_t* __restrict__ cols,\n                                    const index_t* __restrict__ rowDelimiters,\n                                    const double* __restrict__ vec,\n                                    const index_t dim,\n                                    double* __restrict__ out) {\n    const unsigned long long gtid =\n        static_cast<unsigned long long>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const unsigned long long row = gtid / WARP_SIZE;\n    const unsigned int lane = static_cast<unsigned int>(gtid & (WARP_SIZE - 1));\n\n    // The row index is uniform across a warp, so whole warps exit together and\n    // the full-mask shuffles below remain valid.\n    if (row >= dim) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    const index_t start = __ldg(&rowDelimiters[row]);\n    const index_t end = __ldg(&rowDelimiters[row + 1]);\n\n    double t = 0.0;\n    for (index_t j = start + lane; j < end; j += WARP_SIZE) {\n        const index_t col = __ldg(&cols[j]);\n        t += __ldg(&val[j]) * __ldg(&vec[col]);\n    }\n\n    // Warp-level tree reduction of the partial sums\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int offset = WARP_SIZE / 2; offset > 0; offset >>= 1) {\n        t += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, t, offset);\n    }\n\n    if (lane == 0) {\n        out[row] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvGpu\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Host-side launcher for spmvCsrVectorKernel. Performs no host/device\n//   transfers; all operands must already reside on the device.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvGpu(const unsigned long long totalThreads = static_cast<unsigned long long>(dim) * WARP_SIZE;\n    const unsigned int numBlocks =\n        static_cast<unsigned int>((totalThreads + THREADS_PER_BLOCK - 1) / THREADS_PER_BLOCK);\n\n    spmvCsrVectorKernel<<<numBlocks, THREADS_PER_BLOCK>>>(d_val, d_cols, d_rowDelimiters,\n                                                           d_vec, dim, d_out);\n false;\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Check relative error\n            const double relError = std::abs((res - ref) / ref);\n            if (relError > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n    }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of
